chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal from Muhammad ibn Ali from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about al-I'tikaf (seclusion in mosque) in Ramadan during the ten days. He said: Indeed Ali (peace be upon him) used to say: I do not see al-I'tikaf except in the Sacred Mosque or the Messenger's Mosque or in a congregational mosque.

key_terms.العَشر: The ten days: specifically referring to the last ten days of Ramadan
key_terms.المَسجِدِ الحَرَام: Al-Masjid al-Haram: the Sacred Mosque in Mecca
key_terms.الِاعتِكَاف: I'tikaf: spiritual retreat or seclusion in a mosque for worship
key_terms.رَمَضَانَ: Ramadan: the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar
key_terms.مَسجِدِ الرّسُول: Masjid al-Rasul: the Prophet's Mosque in Medina

ai.seo_question: Where should I perform I'tikaf during Ramadan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Istibsar* highlights the scholarly preference for performing I'tikaf exclusively within the three holiest mosques—Al-Masjid al-Haram, Al-Masjid al-Nabi, and a major Jami' mosque—rather than in any general prayer space. By attributing this strict view to Imam Ali (AS), the hadith underscores the elevated spiritual status of these specific sanctuaries in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing them from ordinary mosques for the purpose of this specific act of worship.
